title: The End of the Season
statement: I met Barbora at the beginning of the year at one of Prague’s markets, where she was selling her ceramics. Later it turned out that ceramics were only part of her work. Barbora revives traditional crafts: she tans leather and sheepskins and works with wool. This summer she spent several months as a shepherdess, grazing a flock of sheep and goats on the steppe slopes of Písečný vrch, in the southern part of the Central Bohemian Uplands.

This is a place with a very long memory. Písečný vrch is considered one of the most important Palaeolithic sites in Central Europe: people lived on this hill long before farming, and herding itself, appeared. Today it is a nature reserve, and the flock on its slopes continues the bond between people, animals and land that once shaped this landscape.

The series was made during the last weeks of the grazing season. “Little by little, I began to feel that I wasn’t just someone looking after the flock,” Barbora writes. “I was actually part of it.” The wool and sheepskins she has been processing for several years gained, for the first time, a concrete origin: the animals’ personalities, their behaviour, their life together as a flock. “Living side by side with animals, as I found out, is an elementary thing that I will always need in my life,” she says, “together with creating from what they offer me.”

In the photographs this connection is visible directly. Pasture, dogs, flock and hands with a spindle line up into a single chain, in which the material has not yet separated from the animal, nor the craft from the landscape. It is a story about belonging to a place — lived not as an idea, but as a daily responsibility for living beings.
